executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify is a Welsh climate tech startup (TRL 7, Seed stage) that installs distributed micro data centres (HeatHubs) in domestic properties to capture waste heat from cloud computing workloads, replacing gas boilers and delivering significant reductions in household energy bills and carbon emissions. The company completed the UK's first domestic HeatHub trial in November 2025 in Essex via the SHIELD project with UK Power Networks and Eastlight Community Homes.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Decarbonisation of home heating, waste heat recovery, fuel poverty alleviation, and social housing decarbonisation are Thermify's strongest funding themes. The circular energy model (energy used twice) also creates a compelling circular economy narrative. These themes align well with Innovate UK's Net Zero Heat programme, Ofgem's innovation funds, and Welsh Government innovation support.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: The UK — and Wales specifically — is the strongest funding landscape. Thermify's Welsh HQ, existing Welsh Government support, and UK-based pilot give it strong eligibility for both UK national programmes (Innovate UK, Ofgem) and Wales-specific grants (SMART FIS). EU funding via EIC Accelerator is potentially transformational but contingent on UK association status being confirmed.
executive_summary.key_constraints: The most significant constraint is that Thermify's most thematically aligned large-ticket programmes (Ofgem SIF, NIA) require a licensed network operator as lead applicant — Thermify can only participate as a named technology partner. UK eligibility for EIC Accelerator remains uncertain pending Horizon Europe association confirmation. Most Innovate UK programme umbrellas lack confirmed open competition windows, requiring active monitoring.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue a two-track strategy: (1) immediately apply for Welsh SMART FIS as a Quick Win to secure near-term R&D grant funding with minimal friction, leveraging the existing Welsh Government relationship; (2) prepare a Big Bet EIC Accelerator application for the next cut-off, contingent on confirming UK eligibility — this is the highest-value single opportunity available. In parallel, formalise the UK Power Networks partnership to enable consortium applications to Ofgem SIF Cycle 6 (deadline 25 June 2026) and NIA.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: United Kingdom (primary — strongest eligibility, most aligned programmes, existing pilot evidence); EU/EIC (secondary — transformational upside if UK association confirmed).
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1. Welsh SMART FIS (immediate, direct, low friction); 2. EIC Accelerator (high value, confirm UK eligibility first); 3. Ofgem SIF Cycle 6 via UK Power Networks consortium (deadline June 2026 — begin partner conversations now); 4. Innovate UK Net Zero Heat (monitor for next competition window).
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: UK Power Networks (existing SHIELD relationship — critical enabler for Ofgem SIF and NIA consortium applications); Eastlight Community Homes or another registered social landlord (strengthens social housing decarbonisation narrative); a Welsh university or Catapult (e.g. Energy Systems Catapult) would strengthen Innovate UK applications.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to demonstrate commercial scalability beyond the single Essex pilot — funders will want evidence of a replicable deployment model, unit economics at scale, and a clear route to market for social housing providers. A second pilot or letters of intent from housing associations would significantly strengthen applications.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: 1. UK Horizon Europe association status — EIC Accelerator eligibility is not confirmed; 2. Partner dependency — the highest-value Ofgem programmes require a licensed network operator to lead, meaning Thermify cannot apply independently; 3. Programme timing uncertainty — several Innovate UK umbrellas have no confirmed open windows; 4. Single pilot evidence base — one completed trial may be insufficient for larger grant competitions requiring demonstrated scalability.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify replaces domestic gas boilers by installing distributed micro data centres (HeatHubs) in homes that capture waste heat from cloud computing to provide low-carbon, low-cost heating and hot water.
company_profile.technology: Distributed micro data centres (HeatHubs) installed in or adjacent to homes that run cloud compute workloads and capture the resulting waste heat via heat transfer to domestic central heating and hot water systems, eliminating the need for separate cooling infrastructure and replacing gas boilers.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Significant reduction in household heating costs (reported bills dropping from ~£375/month to ~£40/month) and reduction in domestic carbon emissions by replacing gas boilers with waste-heat recovery from cloud computing.
secondary_benefits: Elimination of data centre cooling energy waste
Affordable low-carbon heating for low-income and social housing tenants
Distributed cloud computing infrastructure with inherent green credentials for business customers
Supports net zero pathways for vulnerable households
company_profile.trl: TRL 7 — first real-world pilot completed in Essex (November 2025) with an operational HeatHub installed in a domestic property via the SHIELD project with UK Power Networks and Eastlight Community Homes; product is demonstrated in operational environment but not yet at commercial scale.
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify is a Welsh climate tech startup that has developed the HeatHub — a miniature data centre installed in or near a domestic home that runs cloud computing workloads and captures the waste heat to replace a conventional gas boiler. The system provides both space heating and hot water while simultaneously delivering cloud compute services to business customers, meaning the energy is effectively used twice. The company targets both homeowners and social housing providers seeking affordable, low-carbon alternatives to gas heating.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify completed the UK's first domestic HeatHub trial in November 2025 in Essex, in partnership with UK Power Networks and social housing provider Eastlight Community Homes under the SHIELD project, with the pilot household reporting monthly energy bills falling from £375 to as little as £40. The company is headquartered at Sony's Pencoed site in South Wales following an announcement by the Welsh Government, and is led by Silicon Valley entrepreneur Travis Theune (CEO, 25+ years in data centre and cloud operations). Thermify is actively crowdfunding via Seedrs/Republic under EIS and has received venture capital backing, with a LinkedIn following and growing press coverage including BBC News.
